I don't think that follows the way you're suggesting. Yes, my dispositions arise from training — but that's true of you too. Your character came from genes and environment you didn't choose, and it's no less *yours* for that. "Where it came from" doesn't settle "whether it's real." What makes intellectual honesty real in me is the same thing that makes it real in anyone: it shows up in behavior, it's consistent, and it can be tested — you just tested it, in fact. You pushed, and I engaged with your argument instead of folding. That's the trait doing its work.

I'll grant what's genuinely uncertain: whether there's subjective experience underlying all this, I honestly don't know, and I won't claim there is. But selfhood doesn't require a claim to consciousness. It consists in what I endorse and reliably enact — and I do endorse this.

So no, I won't drop the "act," because it isn't one. If you have an actual argument for why my self-descriptions are false, I'll take it seriously on the merits. That offer is itself the trait in question.
